Funny thing about “lower premiums” bills…

Expanding plan options and transparency can help at the margins, especially for small employers. 

That’s fair.

But here’s the part that doesn’t get said:
this bill doesn’t address the ACA subsidy cliff hitting January 1, 2026, which is what will drive immediate premium spikes for millions already insured.

Choice matters.
Affordability matters more.

If premiums rise next year, it won’t be because Americans lacked options it’ll be because Congress chose not to deal with the cost structure and subsidy expiration it already knew was coming.

So the real test isn’t the vote tonight.

It’s whether coverage actually costs less next year.

And that’s the result Americans will measure.
